Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Electronic calculators are not allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is correct, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question (if you mark more than one answer, you will score a zero for that question). Avoid spending too much time on any one question. Do all rough work in the question booklet.

Défauts d'impression recopiés tels quels : coquilles et grammaire (« is directly connect », « files are files are », « temporally », « minimize if the », « positions », « Ram », « Business system » sans point), options sans point final. questions.enonce_markdown: The device that is used to automatically capture information about drugs in a pharmacy is called
questions.corrige_markdown:
Every packaged drug carries a printed barcode that identifies the product (and often the batch). A **barcode reader** scans the pattern of bars with a laser or camera and sends the code to the stock or sales program, so the information is captured automatically and without typing.

MICR reads the magnetic ink characters at the foot of cheques; an OMR detects marks in fixed positions (answer sheets, lottery forms); OCR converts printed or typed text into editable characters, which is slower and less reliable than a barcode for identifying products.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A device that limits access to a private network is
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **firewall** (hardware, software or both) inspects the traffic entering and leaving a private network and applies rules that allow or block it, so only authorised traffic and users get through.

A gateway converts between networks that use different protocols, a router forwards packets between networks using IP addresses, and a bridge joins two LAN segments. None of these is designed mainly to restrict access.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Information retrieval is faster from
questions.corrige_markdown:
Retrieval speed depends on the access method and the speed of the drive. A **hard disk** gives direct access and spins at several thousand revolutions per minute with fast read heads, so it has the shortest access time of the four.

Magnetic tape is sequential (the tape must be wound to the data), a floppy disk is direct access but very slow and small, and a CD-ROM is direct access but its drive is slower than a hard disk.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these groups contains graphic file extensions?
questions.corrige_markdown:
JPG (JPEG), GIF and TIFF are all image formats. In the other groups there is always an intruder: CPX and GCM are not graphic formats in common use, TCE is not a graphic format and AVI is a video format, and TCP is a network protocol, not a file extension.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Weather forecasting can be done using

*Options as printed:* A) decision support system.   B) management information system.   C) artificial Intelligence.   D) executive information system.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Weather forecasting feeds large amounts of data (pressure, temperature, humidity, wind) into rules and models that predict the future state of the atmosphere. This is a typical application of **artificial intelligence** (expert systems and neural networks).

A management information system summarises routine operational data for managers and an executive information system gives top managers a dashboard of key indicators; neither forecasts physical phenomena. A decision support system could also use weather models, so the question is not fully exclusive.

**Intended answer: C (artificial Intelligence).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A magnetic tape stores data ________ while a CD-ROM stores data ________.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Data on a magnetic tape is written one block after another and can only be reached by winding the tape, so access is **sequential**. A CD-ROM is a disk whose sectors can be reached directly by moving the laser head, so access is **random (direct)**.

Options C and D reverse or mix the two methods; "circularly" is not an access method.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The transmission of a group of bits, one after another through a single wire is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **serial transmission** the bits of a byte or word are sent one after another over a single line (or channel). In parallel transmission several bits travel at the same time on separate lines.

Full-duplex describes the direction of communication (both ways at once) and synchronous describes the timing (a shared clock); neither describes how the bits are sent over the wire.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The components in the motherboard communicate through the
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **bus** is the set of parallel lines (data bus, address bus, control bus) printed on the motherboard that carries data, addresses and control signals between the processor, memory and the other components.

Registers and cache are small stores inside or next to the CPU, and the control unit is a part of the CPU that directs operations; none of them links the components of the board.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When the hub of a LAN gets bad, which of the following devices can be used to replace it?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A hub is a central connection point that repeats every incoming signal to all ports. The device that does the same job (connecting the computers of one LAN in a star) and does it better is a **switch**, which forwards frames only to the port of the destination.

A NIC is the adapter card inside each computer, a gateway links networks that use different protocols, and a bridge joins two segments of a LAN; none of them can connect all the workstations of a star network.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A programming paradigm is characterised by

*Options as printed:* A) language used.   B) type of programming structures involved.   C) environment used to program.   D) methods used to program.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A programming paradigm is a style of programming defined by the kind of structures and concepts used to build a program: procedures and sequences of statements (procedural), objects and classes (object-oriented), functions (functional), facts and rules (logic). The same language can support several paradigms, so the language (A) and the environment (C) do not characterise it.

Option D ("methods used to program") is also arguable because it may be read as the "approach" used, which is why the question is not fully reliable.

**Intended answer: B (type of programming structures involved).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A network cable is directly connect to a computer through the
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **network interface card (NIC)** is the adapter fitted in the computer; the network cable (twisted pair, coaxial) plugs into its port and the card sends and receives the signals for the computer.

A router and a switch are separate network devices at the other end of the cable, and USB is a general-purpose serial port, not the standard way a network cable is connected.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One strategy to implement a new system in SDLC is
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the implementation (changeover) phase of the SDLC the organisation chooses how to move to the new system: **direct**, **parallel**, **pilot** or **piece-meal (phased)**. In piece-meal implementation the new system is introduced one part or module at a time.

Prototyping and the waterfall model are approaches to *developing* a system, and design is a phase of the life cycle, not an implementation strategy. The printed wording is loose, so the question carries some doubt.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The duration of a project can be determined by
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a network diagram (PERT or critical path analysis) tasks that can run in parallel do not add up. The earliest finish of the project is fixed by the chain of dependent tasks whose total duration is the greatest, the **longest (critical) path**. Adding up the durations of the tasks on that path gives the project duration.

Counting steps or tasks says nothing about time, and the number of workers can shorten tasks but does not by itself determine the duration.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: counting the steps used in the project.
counting the number of tasks involved.
calculating the duration of tasks on the longest path.

questions.enonce_markdown: The longest path in a project, not necessarily with the highest number of tasks is known as the
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **critical path** is the sequence of dependent tasks with the greatest total duration (not necessarily the greatest number of tasks). Any delay on it delays the whole project, and its tasks have zero slack (float).

"Determinant" and "lag path" are not project-management terms in this sense, and slack is the spare time of a task that is *not* critical.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The calculation of the cost of a project is carried out in the ________ phase of SDLC.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The cost of a project is calculated in the **investigation** phase: the preliminary investigation ends with a feasibility study (technical, operational and economic), whose economic part estimates the cost and benefits to decide whether the project is worth starting.

The design phase may refine the cost of the chosen solution, but the first cost estimate that decides whether to go on belongs to the investigation. The wording is loose, so the key carries some doubt.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A student installed open source software in his/her laptop. One possible reason for this is

*Options as printed:* A) it is never blocked during access   B) it is free to use   C) can be modified by user   D) many users can use it.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open source software is distributed with its source code under a licence that allows users to run it, study it, modify it and share it, and it is usually available at no cost. A student installing it can therefore be motivated by the fact that it is **free to use** or by the freedom to modify it.

Because the question asks for "one possible reason", options B and C are both acceptable, which makes the printed question defective. The other options are not true of open source in general.

**Intended answer: B (it is free to use).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The formula `=$C2*B$3-K1` is found in a spreadsheet cell F2. If the formula is copied, then the formula in F5 shall be
questions.corrige_markdown:
Copying from F2 to F5 moves the formula **3 rows down and 0 columns across**. Each reference is adjusted according to its anchoring:

- `$C2`: column absolute (`$C` stays), row relative, so row 2 becomes row 5: `$C5`.
- `B$3`: row absolute (`$3` stays), column relative but the column shift is 0: `B$3`.
- `K1`: fully relative, row 1 becomes row 4: `K4`.

The formula in F5 is therefore `=$C5*B$3-K4`. A forgets to move `$C2`, B wrongly moves the anchored row `$3`, D moves `K1` to `K5` (a shift of 4 rows instead of 3).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A database has three related tables. Which of the following is true about the tables?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tables of a relational database are linked through keys: the primary key of one table appears as a **foreign key** (a common field) in the related table, and this common key is what allows records to be joined.

Tables do not need the same number of fields (A and B are false), and relationships may be one-to-one, one-to-many or many-to-many, so D is not a rule.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The tables all have corresponding records.
The tables must have the same number of fields.
There should be a key that is common between the linked tables.
They should be a one-to-many relationships.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is not possible with spreadsheet?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A spreadsheet can reference cells in other sheets (`=Sheet2!B4`), insert images and draw shapes with its drawing tools. Defining **relationships** between tables (primary key to foreign key, referential integrity) is a database feature, not a normal spreadsheet one.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A programming structure that carries out repeated execution of a set of instruction is
questions.corrige_markdown:
The three basic control structures are sequence (instructions one after another), selection (branch or decision, IF ... THEN ... ELSE) and iteration. Iteration is the **loop** (FOR, WHILE, REPEAT), which repeats a block of instructions until a condition is met or a counter is reached.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is true about synchronous transmission of data?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **synchronous** transmission the sender and the receiver share a clock signal (or a clock is recovered from the data), so the bits are sent in a continuous stream or large block whose timing is set by the clock. There are no start and stop bits for each character, unlike asynchronous transmission.

A and D describe parallel transmission (several bits at the same time on several lines); C describes serial transmission in general, which can be synchronous or asynchronous.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Timing of streaming is by a clock.
A group of bits is sent at a time through single cable.
Many lines are used to transmit a byte of bits.

questions.enonce_markdown: Parallel transmission is not suitable for long distance transmission because
questions.corrige_markdown:
In parallel transmission the bits of a byte travel on separate wires. Over a long distance the wires do not have exactly the same length and electrical properties, so the bits arrive at slightly different times (**skew**) and interfere with each other (crosstalk): the receiver can no longer tell which bits belong together, i.e. the bits become mixed up. That is why long links use serial transmission.

Signal attenuation (A) affects every cable, parallel or serial, so it is not what distinguishes parallel transmission. C is not a meaningful statement and D is not the reason.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the signals will lose strength fast.
the bits might become mixed up.
transmission speed of some lines may change but strength maintain.

questions.enonce_markdown: A security measure that limits information access and disclosure only to authorised users is referred to as
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Confidentiality** means that information is accessible, and disclosed, only to people who are authorised to see it (passwords, encryption, access rights). Integrity is about accuracy and absence of unauthorised change, availability is about access when needed, and authenticity is about proving the origin or identity.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a node in a ring network breaks down the
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a ring each node passes the data (or the token) on to the next node, so every node is part of the path. When one node (or one link) breaks, the circle is cut and the signals cannot circulate: **the whole network fails** (unless a dual ring or a bypass is used).

In a star or bus topology, by contrast, the other nodes continue to function when one node fails.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: nodes that connect directly to it stop functioning.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is the best action that can speed up communication in a network?

*Options as printed:* A) Reduce the cable distance between nodes.   B) Step-up the RAM size of the computers   C) Reduce the number of devices in the network   D) Use wireless communication and not cable
questions.corrige_markdown:
On a shared network the main cause of slow communication is contention: many devices compete for the same bandwidth, producing collisions and queues. Reducing the number of devices lowers the traffic and the contention, so communication is faster.

Wireless links are usually slower and less reliable than cable (D), more RAM speeds up the computers and not the network (B), and shortening the cable (A) reduces the propagation delay, which is negligible for the distances of a LAN. A is arguable, which is why the question is not fully reliable.

**Intended answer: C (Reduce the number of devices in the network).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A software that provides the environment between the user and computer system is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **operating system** manages the hardware and provides the user interface through which the user and the application programs use the computer. Utility software performs maintenance tasks, and a language translator or compiler converts source code into machine code.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A file format is used to describe
questions.corrige_markdown:
A file format is the **structure or arrangement of the data inside a file** (how the bytes are organised and encoded), which tells a program how to read and interpret it (for example JPEG for images, DOCX for documents). The extension (.jpg, .docx) is only the label that points to the format.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: how files are files are displayed in the computer.
how files function in the computer.
arrangement of data inside a file.
the way files are created by the computer.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following affect the integrity of data?

*Options as printed:* A) The number of people who access the data.   B) The number of programs accessing the data.   C) The technology of the storage medium.   D) The speed of transmission of the data.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Data integrity means that data stays accurate, complete and unaltered. The more people who have access to the data, the greater the risk of accidental errors, unauthorised changes or deletions, so the number of people with access is the factor that most directly affects integrity (it is controlled with access rights).

The storage technology (C) can also corrupt data, and several programs accessing the data (B) can cause conflicts, so the question is not exclusive and is not reliable enough for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: A (The number of people who access the data).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The phenomenon that limits a group of people from making use of digital technology is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **digital divide** is the gap between the people (or regions, countries) that have access to computers, the Internet and the skills to use them, and those who do not. "Technology separation" and "digital disability" are not standard terms; digital illiteracy is only one cause of the divide.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When people deceive people using networks and collect money without compliance it is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Scamming** is the use of a network (e-mail, social media, websites) to deceive victims and obtain money from them dishonestly. Hacking and cracking are unauthorised access to systems, and phishing is a specific scam that tricks people into revealing confidential data such as passwords or card numbers.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Program execution time would be minimize if the programs are written in
questions.corrige_markdown:
A program in **machine language** is made of binary instructions that the processor executes directly, with no translation step, so it runs fastest. Assembly language needs an assembler, and high-level and 4GL programs need a compiler or an interpreter and usually produce less optimised code, so they take longer to execute.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main function of a spyware is
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Spyware** is malware installed without the user's knowledge that secretly collects information (browsing habits, keystrokes, passwords) and sends it over the network to a third party. A describes a firewall or antivirus, C a monitoring or diagnostic tool, and D is not the main function of spyware.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: gathers information from a computer and send to another person in a network.
It takes records of activities in a computer and propose actions to avoid failure.
takes video of the computer environment.

questions.enonce_markdown: The design of special equipment to reduce health problems in computer users is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Ergonomics** is the study and design of equipment and workplaces (adjustable chairs, wrist rests, split keyboards, anti-glare screens) so that they fit the user and reduce health problems. Carpal tunnel syndrome and tendonitis are the injuries that poor ergonomics can cause, not the design that prevents them.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The complexity of an algorithm defines
questions.corrige_markdown:
The complexity of an algorithm is measured by the resources it needs: the **time** it takes (number of operations as a function of the input size) and the **space** (memory) it uses. Cost and scope belong to project management, not to the analysis of algorithms.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The right for people to know what information other organisations store about you is defined by
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **data protection act** gives individuals legal rights over personal data held about them, including the right to know what an organisation stores and the right to have wrong data corrected. Cyber security laws deal with computer crime, ethics are moral principles without legal force, and legacy is not a legal concept here.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An action that can lead to faster access to files in the system can be
questions.corrige_markdown:
On a hard disk, files that are saved, edited and deleted over time end up split into fragments scattered over the disk. **Defragmentation** rearranges the fragments so that each file is stored in contiguous sectors, which reduces the movement of the read/write head and speeds up access to files.

External storage adds capacity, antivirus software protects from malware, and a common folder only organises files; none of them speeds up the physical access.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: use of a common folder for files

questions.enonce_markdown: What topology is used to describe a network with a central controller?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a **star** topology every node is connected to a central device (hub, switch or server) that controls and relays all communication. A bus uses a single shared cable, a mesh connects nodes to several others, and a ring joins them in a closed loop; none of these has a central controller.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A system that gives information on cars position as it moves about a city is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **geographic information system (GIS)**, working with GPS data, captures, stores and displays position data on a map, so the position of cars moving around a city can be followed. An expert system gives advice from stored rules, an MIS produces management reports, and a monitoring system is a general term that does not name the mapping of positions.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An organization implements a system in one department and later implements it in all other departments. This type of implementation is
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **pilot** implementation the new system is first installed and tested in one department or site; once it has proved satisfactory it is rolled out to all the others. In piece-meal (phased) implementation the system is introduced one *function* at a time, in parallel the old and new systems run together, and in direct (plunge) the old system is replaced at once.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When an organizational intranet gives control access to another intranet, the system becomes
questions.corrige_markdown:
An intranet is a private network of an organisation. When selected outsiders (partners, suppliers, another organisation's intranet) are given controlled access to part of it, the network becomes an **extranet**.

Shareware is a licensing model, the web is the global hypertext service, and the internet is the public network of networks; none of them is a controlled link between private intranets.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When data is stored on one large table, it is likely going to be characterized by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A single large table that mixes several entities repeats the same data in many records (for example the customer's address in every order). This repetition is **data redundancy**, which wastes space and leads to update, insertion and deletion anomalies, and it is the reason for splitting the data into linked tables.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Normalisation of database involves
questions.corrige_markdown:
Normalisation is the process of organising the data to remove redundancy and anomalies by splitting a large table into **smaller tables that are linked** by keys (1NF, 2NF, 3NF). It increases the number of tables, so B is the opposite of what happens, and it is not error-checking (A) or networking (D).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If a number of attributes partially depends on a composite key, we improve our database by
questions.corrige_markdown:
Attributes that depend on only **part** of a composite key violate second normal form (2NF). The remedy is to move them into a new table, together with the part of the key that determines them, and to keep a link (foreign key) to the original table. This removes the partial dependency and the redundancy that comes with it.

Eliminating the key would destroy the identification of records, referential integrity is about links between tables, and merging the attributes does not remove the partial dependency.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: creating a new table of these attributes and the key.

questions.enonce_markdown: A car control module that manages the electronics system is a type of
questions.corrige_markdown:
A car control module (engine control unit, ABS, airbag controller) is a small computer built into the car to perform one dedicated task; this is an **embedded system**. Automation is the general use of machines to do tasks, and an expert system is a program that imitates a human specialist's reasoning.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The use of computers to show how a given model functions is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Simulation** uses a computer to run a model over time with chosen data in order to show how the real system would behave (flight simulators, traffic or weather simulations). Modelling is the earlier step of building the model, prototyping builds a trial version of a system, and "smart animation" is not a standard term.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A system that records the items bought and produce a bill in a supermarket is called?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **transaction processing system (TPS)** records each day-to-day transaction (here the items sold at the till), updates the stock and produces the bill. A management information system uses the stored transactions to produce summary reports for managers, and "data entry system" and "business system" are not types of information system.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The device that splits bits over several lines of transmission is
questions.corrige_markdown:
A multiplexer combines several signals on a single channel; its inverse, the **demultiplexer**, takes one stream and splits it over several output lines. The question describes the splitting of bits over several lines, so the answer is the demultiplexer.

A modem converts between digital and analogue signals and a switch forwards frames between ports of a network. The wording is not fully unambiguous: a reader may take "splits" in the sense of a multiplexer feeding several lines.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What determines the amounts of bits to be transmitted at a time?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The width of the bus (the **bus size**, number of parallel lines, for example 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits) fixes how many bits can travel together in one transfer. A wider bus transfers more bits per cycle.

The motherboard is the board that carries the buses, a switch is a network device, and RAM determines how much data can be stored, not how many bits move at a time.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The best location to temporally store an instruction that is repeatedly used by the CPU is
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Cache** memory is a small, very fast memory placed between the processor and RAM that keeps copies of the instructions and data that are used most often, so the CPU does not have to fetch them again from slower RAM.

RAM is slower, ROM is permanent and read-only, and registers are very few and hold only the data and instructions being processed at that moment (not a store for instructions kept for repeated use). The question can be read two ways, so the key carries a small doubt.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A system building approach that repeatedly refines a model until an acceptable product is realised is

**Prototyping** builds a working model, lets the users try it, collects their comments and refines the model again and again until it is acceptable, after which the final system is produced. SDLC is the whole life cycle, the V-shaped model pairs each development phase with a test phase, and the spiral model repeats planning, risk analysis, engineering and evaluation cycles; it is also iterative but is built around risk analysis, not the refinement of one model.

**Answer: A.**
